Hydrate, Then Dominate: The Most Ignored Performance Tool

You'll spend an hour planning your workout and forget the one thing that affects every rep of it.

People will research pre-workouts for hours and then walk into training already dry. Water is the cheapest performance upgrade you'll ever get.

Thirst is a late signal

By the time you feel really thirsty, you're usually already behind. Being even a little under-hydrated can make training feel harder than it should — heavier weights, slower pace, foggier focus.

Simple rules that work

  • Start the day with water. Before coffee, before your phone.
  • Drink with every meal. Easy anchor, zero thinking.
  • Carry a bottle. If it's in your hand, it gets used.
  • Check the colour. Pale straw is the goal. Dark means drink up.
  • Long, sweaty session? Consider electrolytes, not just plain water.
Hydrate first. Then go take what's yours.

Don't overdo it either

More isn't always better. Forcing down huge amounts of plain water in a short time — especially during very long endurance events — can be dangerous. Drink steadily, follow your thirst during the day, and top up around training.

Make it automatic

Fill your bottle the night before and put it next to your keys. The best habits are the ones you don't have to remember.

Motivation and fitness for people who'd rather be feared than comfortable.
